ravi-solutions: NexaHealth hit a hard blocker during their on-prem installer on HPE nodes with A100s — installer fails when loading the NVIDIA kernel module. Go-live is next week, can SI team pick this up? @anya-partner-eng
anya-partner-eng: Ack. can you paste the installer/logs and confirm whether this is a marketplace image or a partner-built base image?
ravi-solutions: Partner-built image, RHEL 8.6 kernel 4.18. dmesg shows module version mismatch:
```
[12345.678901] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
[12345.678902] nvidia: version magic '4.18.0-372.el8.x86_64 SMP mod_unload ...'
```
lee-customer-eng: I've uploaded full syslog + node diagnostics to SI ticket SI-2345: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SI-2345
sasha-ops: @anya-partner-eng fyi we've seen the same ABI mismatch in the Aurora SI last quarter. Typical root causes: kernel/driver ABI change or mismatched module build. Options: rebuild modules for target kernel, pin kernel, or use a signed compatibility module. Customer constraints?
matt-sales: Customer leadership flagged this as P1 — they want a mitigation by EOD. Any fast workaround?
anya-partner-eng: Short term: ship a signed precompiled kernel module that matches their kernel. Longer term: add DKMS to the image pipeline so modules rebuild on boot. Need security sign-off for signed modules though.
kira-qa: QA can validate signed-module and DKMS flows. Please add the exact kernel versions and distro matrix to the ticket — we'll run the compatibility matrix.
oliver-arch: Another fallback: use our runtime compat-shim so serving can run in userpace without the proprietary driver for non-GPU workloads. Perf hit but keeps things alive for launch canary. Worth discussing with Nexa.
partner-bot: New support request SI-2345 created and assigned to anya-partner-eng
sasha-ops: Operationally, we can also boot nodes into vendor-provided kernel (5.x) from rescue to unblock inference until a proper module is pushed. Not ideal for production but buys time.
anya-partner-eng: I'll open a driver ops ticket with HW partner contact (NVIDIA: j.gupta@nvidia.com) and request a signed module artifact. Copying @security for module signing requirements.
security: We need to run an SPLA/scoping review before accepting externally-signed kernel modules. Share the signing key plan and CI provenance for the artifact.
ravi-solutions: Thanks — I've pushed full logs to the ticket and noted the rescue-boot mitigation for dev traffic. ETA?
anya-partner-eng: Targeting a temporary signed-module artifact in ~36h for canary testing, with a production-safe pipeline (DKMS + signed modules) early next week. I'll update SI-2345 and ping this thread.
matt-sales: Thanks — I'll keep NexaHealth leadership informed. :thumbsup: 
ravi-solutions: Great. Please loop in hardware partner PM if anything requires vendor QA. I'll stand by and help validate once artifact available.
